name: ai-reviewer
repoRules:
This is the ai-reviewer engine itself: pure ESM (.mjs), Node >= 22, zero runtime dependencies — "add library X" is not a finding but a violation of a declared package property.
Canonical primitives are defined once in lib/util.mjs; index.mjs and lib/structure-evidence.mjs re-export them — that is one API under two names, not duplicated implementation.
Fail-open by default: bin/*.mjs catches any exception and exits 0, exit 1 is only the deliberate gate in runReview; "error swallowed" is not a defect when it concerns an external effect (network, tool, fs).
Truncations (diff chunks, structure_context, maxEntities, prompt limits) are declared and reflected by a truncated/provenance flag; the defect is a truncation WITHOUT the flag or one that leaves dangling references, not truncation as such.
Rust port: rust/src/*.rs deliberately mirrors the JS function one-to-one, and lib/*.mjs keeps a deprecated JS fallback of the same logic for when the binary is absent — matching code in JS↔Rust and wrapper↔fallback pairs is parity, not copy-paste.
Since RFC 20 the Rust prompts (rust/src/prompt.rs) are the primary ones and the deprecated JS prompt copies may differ from them: such a divergence is not a defect, and "extract a shared constant" is not a finding.
The profile (lib/profile.mjs) is a process-wide singleton, read-only after loading; MARKERS in lib/constants.mjs are live getters, not a snapshot. This is deliberate global state, not a forgotten refactoring.
Two kinds of paths: package artifacts are read via pkgPath(), consumer data via profile.paths.* from the working directory. Mixing the two kinds is a defect; having two ways is not.
The gate does not know about the structure contour: pipeline.mjs and lib/*.mjs (except structure-*) do not import structure modules, and structure blocks nothing. "Not integrated into the pipeline" is not a finding.
Structure providers return receipts, not a verdict; the statuses covered|partial|missing|unverifiable are computed only by the deterministic assessment engine, and the protocol has its own STRUCTURE_PROTOCOL_VERSION.
Part of the logic is declared a heuristic and carries confidence below exact (lcov matching by name, binding a test to a contract by label, test-body boundaries by regex) — "imprecise" without a concrete counterexample in the diff is not a finding.
EXPORT_VERSION grows on additive changes too: the consumer must check "version is known", not equality.
A finding's route (inline or summary) is computed from the sum of deterministic signals in lib/actionability.mjs and is deliberately separated from the blocking decision (severity/REVIEW_BLOCK_ON) — do not propose routing by the severity label.
FP patterns in feedback/fp-patterns.jsonl are portable across repositories and therefore must be scoped by requiresPath — a pattern without requiresPath is a defect.
Tests: node --test test/*.test.mjs, each file in its own process (the profile is process-wide); eval without an LLM — npm run eval on fixtures/; gold with an LLM — gold/. A spec next to the change in the diff counts as a test.
Code comments, documentation and commit messages in this repository are written in Russian; LLM prompts and review output are in English.

prompts.aggregatorExtra: A complaint about a decision declared in the project rules above (re-exported primitives, fail-open, declared truncation, a JS↔Rust parity copy, no dependencies) is not a finding at any severity.
prompts.verifierExtra: Reject a blocking severity whose justification comes down to an architectural preference rather than incorrectness visible in the diff itself.
